concept:
Zero-CPU Theme Architecture (Intel HD 4000) 2026-06-20 firefox, css, performance, gpu, intel-hd-4000, theme, optimization, zero-cpu, hardware-acceleration
Strategy for building a Firefox UI theme that consumes 0 CPU cycles during animations. By leveraging specific CSS properties (`transform`, `opacity`), we can offload all animation work to the Intel HD 4000's fixed-function GPU hardware (ASIC), keeping the CPU strictly dedicated to rendering web content.
<hardware_profile> <gpu>Intel HD 4000 (Ivy Bridge, Gen 7)</gpu> <components> <component>16 Execution Units (EUs) — programmable shader cores</component> <component>Fixed-Function Transform Unit — matrix math (transforms)</component> <component>ROP (Raster Operations Pipeline) — alpha blending (opacity)</component> <component>TMU (Texture Mapping Unit) — texture/image sampling</component> </components> </hardware_profile>
<rendering_pipeline> <step id="1" name="Style Calc">CPU (Main Thread) - CSS selector matching</step> <step id="2" name="Layout">CPU (Main Thread) - Box model, positioning</step> <step id="3" name="Paint">CPU (Main Thread) - Rasterize elements into texture tiles</step> <step id="4" name="Composite">GPU (Compositor Thread) - Assembles pre-baked textures</step> <target>Our theme must live entirely in Step 4 to achieve zero-CPU overhead.</target> </rendering_pipeline>
<css_rules> <approved_properties type="GPU Native"> Pure matrix multiply (Fixed-Function Unit) Pure matrix multiply (Fixed-Function Unit) Hardware blend (ROP Alpha Blend Unit) Simple per-pixel math (Execution Units) </approved_properties>
<forbidden_properties type="CPU Reflow Triggers"> Triggers full layout recalculation Cascades box model changes through DOM Box model change Positional reflow Forces monitoring of layout properties Heavy compositing pass (GPU, but expensive) </forbidden_properties> </css_rules>
<golden_rules> Only animate `transform` and `opacity` properties. Use `will-change: transform;` on interactive elements to pre-promote them to dedicated GPU compositor layers. Use `contain: strict;` to isolate paint regions and prevent repaints from rippling outward. </golden_rules>
